events.continuity_hook: Continues the DC family trip after Maya checks the school calendar and her spouse's time off.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the DC flights and hotel area to one approval-ready family plan with the main tradeoffs clearly summarized.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's spouse confirms they can take the full four-night early-April trip, with a preference for arriving before dinner on the first day and returning after lunch on the last day. DCA remains the easiest airport for the museum-heavy plan, but BWI is still meaningfully cheaper for three tickets once baggage and ground transfer time are considered. The hotel shortlist has narrowed to a Penn Quarter property with larger rooms and many restaurants nearby, a Smithsonian-area hotel with included breakfast but tighter rooms, and a Capitol Hill option that is quieter but less convenient for their first two museum days. The remaining decisions are airport choice, whether the room-size advantage outweighs free breakfast, and how late a return flight is comfortable for their child before the school week resumes.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the DC plan from comparison into booking before the airfare changes again.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the DC flights and hotel, note the family seating plan, and capture the practical booking details.
events.scenario_brief: The family decides to use DCA despite the higher fare because it keeps the arrival and departure days simpler, and the Penn Quarter hotel becomes the preferred stay because the larger room and easy dinner access matter more for four nights than included breakfast. The preferred outbound is a late-morning nonstop from Atlanta that arrives with time to settle in before an easy first evening, and the return is an early-afternoon nonstop that avoids both a rushed hotel checkout and a late school-night arrival. The hotel rate is cancellable, breakfast is paid, and the property can note a quiet-room request. The remaining items are booking the three tickets together, selecting seats with Maya in a window seat if the map allows, adding the hotel request, and saving confirmation details for the family budget.

events.continuity_hook: Final family-trip logistics pass after the DC bookings are in place and museum times are set.
events.interaction_goal: Turn the DC itinerary into a concise departure checklist and decide whether any seat or ground-transfer changes are worthwhile.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the DC trip, the flights and Penn Quarter hotel are booked, but the airline has adjusted the outbound arrival slightly later and the family wants to make sure the first evening still works. The hotel confirms luggage storage if the room is not ready, breakfast remains paid, and several casual dinner options are within a short walk. Timed museum entries are now set for two mornings, and the forecast suggests carrying light rain gear. The open items are airport arrival timing in Atlanta, whether to prebook the DCA transfer or use rideshare on arrival, how to handle breakfast on the first full morning, and whether any better family seat grouping has opened.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new work-travel episode once the April family trip is finished and a May client request arrives.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Raleigh trip, identify the practical flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details needed before approval.
events.scenario_brief: After the DC family trip, Maya is asked to plan a solo May client visit to Raleigh for go-live preparation. The likely pattern is a Monday arrival, Tuesday and Wednesday onsite build sessions, and a Thursday return, but the client has not yet confirmed whether the work will be at the hospital campus near downtown or at a suburban administrative office. Atlanta to RDU has several nonstop options, while one-stop fares are only modestly cheaper and would add unnecessary connection risk. She wants a hotel that keeps the mornings easy, has solid guest ratings, and offers workable dinner options without renting a car if the main site is downtown. The unresolved pieces are the exact worksite, first required onsite time, Thursday wrap-up time, and whether the client will recommend rideshare, shuttle, or a rental car.

events.continuity_hook: Continues Raleigh planning after the client confirms the downtown campus and session times.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight and hotel combinations and choose the package Maya should send for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the downtown hospital campus, a Tuesday 8:30 a.m. start, a full Wednesday working session, and a Thursday closeout expected to finish by 12:30 p.m. The best outbound is a Monday late-morning nonstop that allows hotel check-in and a preparation block, while the cheapest one-stop option adds a connection and arrives too late to be useful. For Thursday, a midafternoon nonstop is possible but tight if the closeout slips, while an early-evening nonstop gives more breathing room before heading to the airport. Hotel options include a highly rated downtown hotel with on-site dining and paid breakfast, a limited-service property with included breakfast but a less convenient morning commute, and a lower-rate airport-area hotel that would make both onsite mornings more complicated.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Raleigh work trip from approval into booking while the selected fare and hotel rate are still available.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Raleigh flights, hotel, local transportation notes, room request, seat choices, and receipt capture.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Monday late-morning nonstop, the early-evening Thursday return, and the downtown hotel as long as the room remains cancellable. The client confirms that rideshares are normal for airport and campus transfers, so no rental car is needed. The hotel can add a quiet-room request away from elevators, breakfast is not included, and there are early cafes nearby. Seat maps show a few window seats toward the rear of both flights, while the forward cabin has mostly aisle and middle seats left. The remaining items are completing the booking before the fare hold expires, choosing seats, noting the no-car plan, and saving receipt details for reimbursement.
